text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: elevated error rate (5xx / request signing) across auth service and multiple worker startups. Root cause suspected: external KMS API latency/timeouts (AWS KMS in us-west-2, possible GCP KMS spikes in europe-west1). PagerDuty P1 triggered.

pagerduty: Paging now: escalation to primary on-call @maria-oncall, 2 min to acknowledge.

maria-oncall: acked. joining. seeing alerts for Service=auth, Job=worker-init failing with key retrieval timeouts. Can someone paste representative logs?

ben-sre: paste from logs:
```
2026-03-15T01:12:42Z auth-service ERROR signer: failed to fetch key from KMS: request failed: 504 Gateway Timeout
2026-03-15T01:12:42Z worker-init ERROR bootstrap: cannot initialize keystore: timeout waiting for KMS GetKey
2026-03-15T01:12:43Z http ERROR /auth/token 500 "Error: signer unavailable (KMS errors)"
```
Seen across multiple AZs in us-west-2 and sporadic traces in europe-west1. Error rate at peak ~18% on token endpoint.

alice-ops: confirmed. I tried rolling restarts on a couple of Dedicated nodes — pods get stuck in CrashLoopBackoff during startup because keystore init blocks. Tried increasing KMS client timeout -> still failing.

carla-eng: quick security note: we have an internal fallback software signer feature (FEATURE_SOFTWARE_SIGNER) meant for emergencies — it uses vended ephemeral keys cached locally. It reduces exposure window but must be rotated quickly. We should get approvals before enabling org-wide.

maria-oncall: customer impact? which customers hit 5xxs? any enterprise tenants?

tim-support: quick count from logs: ~23 distinct customers had token errors in last 30m; 4 enterprise Dedicated tenants reported onboarding failures (support tickets opened). One high-rev partner reported API failures for auth flows. Created support ticket: INC-2026-4321 and flagged as P1.

ben-sre: runbook proposal (short):
1) Enable FEATURE_SOFTWARE_SIGNER for 10% of fleet (canary) in us-west-2 only via console feature flag API.
2) If canary stable for 10m (error rate drop to <2%), sweep to remaining Dedicated & Private nodes.
3) Open high-priority ticket with AWS KMS (case 1234567891) and attach traces.
4) If KMS errors persist >30m, route affected requests to regional fallback KMS endpoint (configurable) and add circuit-breaker to avoid floods.

alice-ops: starting canary now. command to flip flag:
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal.api/flags \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"flag":"FEATURE_SOFTWARE_SIGNER","value":true,"scope":"us-west-2","percent":10}'
```
Executing...

alice-ops: :hourglass_flowing_sand: canary flipped; rolling out to 10% of worker pods in us-west-2. Monitoring metrics.

ben-sre: also enabling short-lived cache for KMS responses (ttl=30s) on canary to reduce calls. command: `kubectl set env deployment/auth-worker KMS_CACHE_TTL=30`

carla-eng: adding encryption team: enabling software signer increases signing surface but avoids customer downtime. We're ok with 10% canary. Prepare rotation script to run every 15m to revoke ephemeral keys once KMS recovers.

maria-oncall: pinging AWS status and opening support case. aws support case created: 1234567891. AWS showed "elevated KMS latencies" in us-west-2 on status page: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — posted update at 01:18Z.

tim-support: posted customer advisory to status.redwood.com: "We are investigating intermittent authentication failures caused by upstream KMS latency. Some Dedicated and Private deployments may experience startup errors and token failures. Temporary mitigation in progress."

alice-ops: canary metrics update (01:27Z): token 5xx rate on canary nodes dropped from 18% -> 1.8%. on non-canary still ~13%.

ben-sre: good. expanding canary to 40% in us-west-2. flipping feature to 40%.

alice-ops: rolling to 40% now. applying additional config to avoid retry storms: `KMS_MAX_RETRIES=2` and `KMS_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=250`.

maria-oncall: executing oncall handoff: I'm handing active incident to @ben-sre (sre night lead) at 01:45Z for follow-up and vendor coordination. Leaving notes: canary stable, expansion in progress, AWS case open.

ben-sre: acked and taking over. I'll coordinate with cloud support and security for rotation plan. Next steps: escalate with AWS if latencies don't improve in 20m. Also prepare rollback plan to disable software signer if we detect misuse/attacks.

carla-eng: prepping rotation script and a short audit log toggle `LOG_SOFTWARE_SIGNER_ACTIVATION=true`. Make sure we capture which nodes used the fallback.

tim-support: customer update: updated P1 tickets with mitigation steps and ETA: 45m to full mitigation for most customers.

incidents-bot: Update: 01:58Z — automated metric check: error rate now 2.1% cluster-wide, 0.9% on nodes with fallback. Keeping incident open pending AWS resolution.

ben-sre: AWS responded to case: KMS team acknowledges elevated latencies due to internal throttling in region; they're applying capacity relief. ETA from AWS: 30-60m. They asked for request traces (uploaded).

alice-ops: sweeping remaining us-west-2 fleet to enable fallback (now at 95%). europe-west1 left untouched for now (lower impact).

tim-support: customers reporting improved behavior, one enterprise tenant says their onboarding is now succeeding again.

ben-sre: recommended post-incident actions (PIA):
- Add regional KMS latency alerting (SLO breach early-warning).
- Document and test software signer fallback in staging + regular drills.
- Add cached key layer with secure TTL and automated rotation.
- Add runbook entry for toggling feature flags and safe rollouts.
- Follow up with AWS for RCA and SLA credits.

maria-oncall: thanks team. I'm back on-call, quick handover notes accepted. If anything regresses ping me.

carla-eng: security note: we will run a key-rotation and audit for any ephemeral keys used as fallback. schedule Exec review if needed.

incidents-bot: 02:30Z — incident status: mitigated (customer impact reduced, fallback in place). Incident remains open for postmortem and vendor RCA.

ben-sre: marking primary mitigation complete. I will own the postmortem; creating doc: /incidents/postmortems/2026-03-15-kms-latency.md. Will include timeline, decisions, and follow-ups.

tim-support: sending final customer note: "We implemented a temporary local key fallback while AWS remediated KMS latency; services are recovering. We will follow up with a full postmortem." :white_check_mark:
